note_on_reviewer_fallback_already_invite: The chained r1_review.json for the same 0704-070402 round explicitly said: 'Replace the adjudication artifact with one that mechanically applies an already-registered Δpp threshold, if such a valid prior registration exists.' This ruling exercises exactly that fallback; it does not overrule or contradict the reviewer.
human_ruling: The reviewer's REVISE verdict at .orchestrate/0704-070402 was correct on the facts available to it: the executor's decision artifact used an unregistered mean±std band heuristic, not a preregistered rule, and no valid Delta-pp registration was visible from inside the repository. This ruling does not overturn that finding. What has changed is that a genuine preregistration was located outside the repository: vault card `bm3-secondary-ablation-decide.md` (created 2026-07-03, in `/mnt/c/Users/ThinkPad/Obsidian Vault/`), corroborated word-for-word by an independent `log.md` entry dated the same day, both predating the grid's 2026-07-03T10:34 start by the ordering documented in `prereg_provenance.md`. The automated reviewer could not have found this: `run_codex_review()` in `/home/jeffwork/exp/physics-mechanism/orchestrate.py` passes the reviewer only the card's RUBRIC section plus the git workdir's contents, never the card's TASK section (where the concrete 8pp/[3,8)pp/collapse-to-s4d rule lives) and never the external vault path. That is a structural scope limitation of the review harness, not a mistake by the reviewer. Given the reviewer's own stated fallback -- apply an already-registered Delta-pp threshold if one is found to exist -- the correct resolution is to materialize that provenance (prereg_provenance.md) and mechanically apply the card's actual rule to the already-frozen aggregate outputs (secondary_decision.json in this directory), without rerunning the grid, without changing any aggregate value, and without touching the 175 raw cells. That is what this directory does. Rerunning the grid, as a literal reading of the reviewer's REVISE might suggest absent this new information, is not necessary once the pre-existing valid registration is on the record. Separately, .orchestrate/0705-160159/r1_review.json (a later scoped review of the first mechanical-rule attempt at results/secondary_adjudication_20260705-1610/) correctly found that the NOT_DRIVER branch of that attempt used an unregistered mean fallback instead of the card's actual per-bin '|Δ| < +3pp' text, that the decision cited a stale reviewer verdict instead of the more recent .orchestrate/0704-215713/r3_review.json, and that this very ruling document quoted a reviewer verdict with an ellipsis instead of the full text. This ruling and its sibling artifacts in this directory fix all three; this ruling does not overturn that review either -- it was correct.
